l4_steps.name: Extract O&D Revenue & Booking Data
l4_steps.input: Seasonal booking history, MIDT data feeds, BSP/ARC settlement files
l4_steps.output: O&D revenue matrix by route, cabin class, and booking window
l4_steps.kpi: Data extract completeness ≥99%; query SLA <4 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT data covers only ~65% of bookings; direct/NDC channel bookings require separate aggregation from Altéa DCS, causing analyst reconciliation overhead

l4_steps.name: Pull Route Operating Cost Data
l4_steps.input: General ledger actuals, cost centre allocations, fuel price feeds
l4_steps.output: Direct operating cost per departure by route and aircraft type
l4_steps.kpi: Cost data refresh lag <24 hrs; CASM variance vs budget <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet commonality (737 family) limits aircraft-type cost granularity; fuel hedging gains/losses allocated at entity level not route level, distorting route CASM

l4_steps.name: Retrieve Competitive Fare Intelligence
l4_steps.input: Competitor SSIM files, OAG traffic data, ATPCO fare tariff feeds
l4_steps.output: Competitive fare matrix and capacity share by route
l4_steps.kpi: Competitor fare coverage ≥90% of routes under review
l4_steps.pain_point: LCC and ULCC competitors file fares with minimal lead time; ATPCO refresh cycle (2x weekly) creates stale data windows that allow mispriced response strategies

l4_steps.name: Validate Data Completeness & Reconcile
l4_steps.input: O&D revenue matrix, cost extract, competitive data, Altéa PNR data
l4_steps.output: Reconciled route data package; data quality scorecard
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation exceptions <1% of route-months; sign-off completed within 1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-system reconciliation between Altéa settlement data and SAP GL actuals regularly surfaces timing differences of 3–5 days for interline and codeshare revenue

l4_steps.name: Analyse Load Factor & Yield by Route
l4_steps.input: Reconciled route data package, cabin inventory records
l4_steps.output: Load factor and yield report by route, DOW, and season
l4_steps.kpi: System-wide load factor target ≥83%; yield degradation alert threshold >5% YoY
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa NRM optimises at O&D level; thin point-to-point routes with no connecting traffic receive less sophisticated demand modelling, leading to premature sell-down

l4_steps.name: Model O&D Traffic Spill & Recapture
l4_steps.input: Load factor report, O&D demand signals, competitor capacity data
l4_steps.output: Spill/recapture estimates; demand elasticity coefficients by route
l4_steps.kpi: Spill model accuracy ≥88% vs actual post-departure; recapture rate assumption validated quarterly
l4_steps.pain_point: Pure point-to-point network means spilled passengers rarely recaptured on connecting itineraries; recapture assumptions borrowed from hub-and-spoke models overstate true recapture by 10–15%

l4_steps.name: Assess Route Against Break-Even Load Factor
l4_steps.input: Yield data, direct operating costs per ASM, average fare
l4_steps.output: Break-even load factor by route; routes flagged for detailed cost review
l4_steps.kpi: Break-even LF calculation completed for 100% of routes under review
l4_steps.pain_point: Break-even LF sensitive to fuel price assumptions; a ±10% fuel swing shifts break-even by 3–4 pp, requiring frequent scenario refreshes that strain analyst bandwidth

l4_steps.name: Attribute Direct Operating Costs to Route
l4_steps.input: Cost centre actuals, block hours by route, fuel consumption by tail
l4_steps.output: Direct CASM (crew, fuel, maintenance, airport fees) per route
l4_steps.kpi: Direct cost attribution covers ≥95% of route operating cost; CASM per ASM variance <1.5¢ vs prior period
l4_steps.pain_point: Maintenance event timing distorts monthly route CASM; an A-check occurring mid-month inflates CASM for that route by 8–12%, masking underlying profitability

l4_steps.name: Allocate Overhead & Indirect Costs to Route
l4_steps.input: Corporate overhead pools (IT, HR, HQ), fleet lease costs, depreciation schedules
l4_steps.output: Fully-loaded CASM per route including overhead allocation
l4_steps.kpi: Overhead allocation methodology reviewed annually; allocation variance <3% across fleet
l4_steps.pain_point: No universally agreed overhead allocation driver; switching from ASM-based to departure-based allocation changes route rankings by up to 15 positions, creating internal disagreement on route verdicts

l4_steps.name: Compare CASM Against Fleet-Type Benchmark
l4_steps.input: Fully-loaded CASM, benchmark CASM by 737 variant (700/800/MAX 8)
l4_steps.output: CASM variance report; routes flagged for gauge optimisation review
l4_steps.kpi: Routes with CASM >110% of fleet benchmark escalated for review
l4_steps.pain_point: 737-700 has ~18% higher CASM per ASM vs MAX 8; routes locked to -700 gauge due to gate constraints or runway length restrictions cannot benefit from gauge upgrades

l4_steps.name: Build Route Contribution Margin P&L Model
l4_steps.input: O&D revenue matrix, direct CASM, overhead allocation, ancillary revenue estimates
l4_steps.output: Route P&L model: RASM, CASM, contribution margin, EBIT per route
l4_steps.kpi: P&L model completed for 100% of routes under review; contribution margin >0 for ≥85% of network routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary revenue (EarlyBird, upgraded boarding, baggage) not disaggregated at route level in Altéa; lump-sum allocation from corporate finance understates ancillary contribution on leisure-heavy routes by up to 20%

l4_steps.name: Run Frequency & Gauge Sensitivity Scenarios
l4_steps.input: Route P&L model, fleet assignment options, schedule constraints from SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Scenario comparison matrix: +1 freq, -1 freq, gauge-up, gauge-down, suspend
l4_steps.kpi: At least 3 scenarios modelled per underperforming route; scenario run time <2 hrs per route
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet commonality reduces gauge flexibility to 737-700 vs 737-800/MAX 8; slot-constrained airports (DCA, LGA) limit frequency increase scenarios regardless of P&L outcome

l4_steps.name: Assess Network Contribution & Connectivity Value
l4_steps.input: Scenario matrix, network connectivity model, Rapid Rewards contribution data
l4_steps.output: Revised profitability ranking incorporating network externality value
l4_steps.kpi: Network contribution adjustment applied to ≥100% of reviewed routes; connectivity premium >5% of direct P&L flagged for executive review
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-to-point model lacks hub feed economics; connectivity value difficult to quantify without connecting passenger data — WN does not sell connecting itineraries through GDS, limiting third-party validation

l4_steps.name: Prepare Route Profitability Scorecard
l4_steps.input: Route P&L models, scenario outputs, competitive benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Executive route profitability dashboard: RAG status, trend, strategic recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard delivered within 5 business days of data extract; dashboard refresh SLA <1 hr
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards sourced from AWS Redshift data lake; ETL pipeline latency of 6–8 hrs means executives sometimes review overnight decisions against stale figures

l4_steps.name: Review Findings with Commercial Leadership
l4_steps.input: Route profitability scorecard, RM yield forecast, Sales channel input
l4_steps.output: Reviewed recommendation with leadership commentary; routes approved/deferred/escalated
l4_steps.kpi: Leadership review completed within 10 business days of analysis; ≥90% of recommendations resolved without escalation to CEO
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue Management and Network Planning use different optimisation horizons (RM: 90-day, NP: 12-18 month); misalignment on route verdicts for routes in near-term yield recovery frequently causes review rework

l4_steps.name: Document Decision & Update Route Status
l4_steps.output: Route status updated in SkyWORKS (Grow/Maintain/Reduce/Suspend); decision audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Route status update completed within 2 business days of approval; 100% of decisions documented with rationale
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS decision log is free-text; no structured field for profitability verdict — audit trail relies on manual documentation discipline, creating compliance risk during DOT reviews
